items.title: Posteryard Brings Clean, Consistent Posters to Plex, Jellyfin, and Emby
items.summary: If you've spent much time organizing a Plex, Jellyfin, or Emby library, you've probably noticed how inconsistent movie and TV posters can look. Some have oversized titles, others are covered in promotional text, and occasionally the artwork looks completely out of place next to everything else. Posteryard is a self-hosted, open-source tool that tackles this problem by automatically generating consistent artwork across your media library. Instead of manually choosing posters for hundreds of titles, it finds suitable artwork, applies a uniform layout, and keeps everything updated as your collection grows.

items.title: Pulse Monitors Your Proxmox and Docker Servers From One Dashboard
items.summary: Keeping an eye on a homelab gets more complicated once you have several machines running different services. Your Proxmox dashboard might show that everything is online, while a Docker container on another server has stopped responding. You could also have a backup that's been failing for days without realizing it. Pulse is a self-hosted monitoring application that collects information from your servers and displays it through a central dashboard. It supports Proxmox, Docker, TrueNAS, and several other platforms, with notifications for problems that might otherwise go unnoticed.

items.title: This is the First Time Astronomers Have Seen One of These Stellar Mergers
items.summary: Some binary stars end up sharing a common envelope of gas, as the primary star draws material away from its companion. The envelope exerts drag on the stars and they can spiral toward each other. In some cases, this creates an eruption or explosion called a luminous red nova. items.title: A game you cannot win unless you have a quantum computer
items.summary: On a superconducting processor, we turned one of quantum mechanics’ strangest features into something you can measure, benchmark, and put to work across systems as large as 105 qubits. Here is a Sunday paper-style puzzle you can try right now. Draw a 3×3 grid. Fill every cell with either +1 or −1, subject to two rules: each row must multiply to +1, and each column must multiply to −1. You didn’t manage it, right? There is an elegant reason for that. For a row to multiply to +1, it needs an even number of −1s.

items.title: NASA’s Voyager 1 Makes History Reaching One Light-Day From Earth
items.summary: NASA’s Voyager 1 probe, humanity’s farthest-flying spacecraft, has reached one light-day from Earth, after more than 49 years of constant travel. A light-day is the distance light travels in 24 hours, equaling about 16.1 billion miles (25.9 billion kilometers). The spacecraft achieved the milestone at 2:16 a.m. PST (5:16 a.m. EST) Nov. 18. Voyager team members at NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory in Southern California, managed by Caltech, heard from the probe 24 hours later, the time it took for the spacecraft’s radio signal traveling at the speed of light to reach Earth, early Thursday.

items.title: Artemis astronauts on the moon will see Earth upside down
items.summary: Artemis astronauts on the moon will see Earth upside down In 2028, the astronauts of Artemis 4 are scheduled to end a more than 50-year absence of humans on the moon’s surface. How will their experience compare with that of the Apollo astronauts? For one thing, Artemis astronauts will see Earth comparatively “upside down.”.Plus, they’ll walk in shadows that stretch for miles. Apollo astronauts visited six different sites that were on the moon’s northern hemisphere or close to the equator. In contrast, Artemis astronauts will be near the south pole, taking advantage of the low angle of the sun, where craters can be in permanent shade and possibly harbor stores of water ice.

items.title: NASA's new Moon plans have a problem: Orion wasn't designed to fly this way
items.summary: NASA recently announced a significant shakeup to the Artemis program that will land humans on the Moon. The moves were designed to give the agency's lunar lander providers—SpaceX with its Starship vehicle, and Blue Origin with Blue Moon—more flexibility in reaching the Moon. For Starship, this means docking with Orion in Earth orbit, and then traveling to the Moon in tandem. For Blue Moon, it shifts the rendezvous with Orion all the way to low-lunar orbit. These changes benefit the lunar landers, but in turn impose more of a burden on the Orion spacecraft, which is built for NASA by Lockheed Martin.

items.title: Einstein was right! Scientists verify 1st image of a black hole ever captured

items.summary: Maricopa County has confirmed 28 measles cases among residents this year, far more than the average of one case a year it has seen over the past 30 years, according to the county Department of Public Health. In a letter to the county Planning and Zoning Commission, Mayes said the panel should wait until state and federal agencies finish reviewing the project. items.title: AI helps researchers investigate how thousands of medical studies share code
items.summary: The data and code that underpin a research study can tell us what was actually done, and how. In a medical study, for example, how were patients selected for inclusion? How were missing values handled? How were the results evaluated? Access to a study's data and code help researchers to answer these questions, to examine the methods, and to build on the work. “Studies involve many choices about how to prepare data, develop models, and evaluate performance. These are sometimes called ‘researcher degrees of freedom,’” says Tom Pollard, a research scientist at MIT's Laboratory for Computational Physiology and Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence Laboratory.

items.title: MCAO attorney who drank at DUI training disciplined, office says
items.summary: PHOENIX (AZFamily) — An attorney with the Maricopa County Attorney’s Office was disciplined for his behavior at an alcohol training event last month, the office said Thursday. In an email statement, Maricopa County Attorney Rachel Mitchell said a “newer” attorney drank alcohol as part of an Oct. 9 training run by outside agencies designed to help officers spot alcohol impairment. Mitchell said volunteers are asked to drink enough to reach a certain blood alcohol level. During this training, Mitchell said the attorney reached a high blood alcohol level and “did not conduct himself in a professional way.”

items.title: White Sands National Park: Things to Do & Where to Camp Nearby
items.summary: Picture this: you wax up a plastic saucer, push off the top of a sugar-white dune, and look up mid-run to see the jagged San Andres Mountains stretched across the horizon. Then you hike back up and do it again. And again, until the sun slips behind those peaks and the whole dunefield glows pink and gold. That’s what happens White Sands National Park, which protects much of the world’s largest gypsum dunefield: 275 square miles of glittering sand in southern New Mexico’s Tularosa Basin. The sand stays cool under bare feet even on warm days, the Sacramento Mountains light up at sunset, and once it’s dark, the stars put on a show of their own.

items.title: ESA's Hera Probe Uses "Superhuman" Vision to Inspect NASA's Asteroid Crash Site
items.summary: Around four years ago, humanity intentionally hit an asteroid. The Double Asteroid Redirection Test (DART) was by pretty much all measures a resounding success when it struck the asteroid moonlet Dimorphos going more than 22,000 kilometers per hour. However, we still don’t know just how much of a success it actually was - DART was a one-way mission with no real way to track the results of the impact close up. Enter Hera, the European Space Agency (ESA) mission that recently arrived in the binary asteroid system. Now, in a press release, ESA has provided some of the best pictures of the binary system since that fateful day four years ago.

items.title: Adaptive AI agent connects experimental planning with robotic control in wastewater treatment test
items.summary: Artificial intelligence systems are now widely used in research settings, primarily to analyze data, make predictions and discover promising materials, drugs or solutions. Most of the agents used for research are disembodied, which means that they are computer-based and require humans or separate automated systems to physically perform experiments.

items.title: In Peacock's 'Dig,' Amy Poehler Plays an Archaeologist Who Discovers an Extraordinary Statue in Greece. What Do Real Experts Think of the TV Series?
items.summary: With their beloved NBC workplace comedy, “ Parks and Recreation,” actor Amy Poehler and series co-creator Michael Schur did the impossible. items.title: Raspberry Pi SBCs get an open-source hardware I2C TPM 2.0 security module (Crowdfunding)
items.summary: ANAVI I2C TPM 2.0 is an open-source hardware I2C TPM 2.0 security module for Raspberry Pi single board computers based on the Infineon Optiga SLB 9673 TPM 2.0 chip. It’s an alternative to the earlier ANAVI TPM 2.0 module using an Optiga SLB 9672 SPI chip. The add-on board is designed for developers, hobbyists, and professionals who require enhanced security for Raspberry Pi-based projects. It’s especially useful for disk encryption, secure key storage, and cryptographic operations, but can also work as a True Hardware Random Number Generator (TRNG) for security-critical applications.

items.title: Rust Coreutils 0.13 Release Delivers More Performance, Better Compatibility
items.summary: Rust Coreutils 0.13 released today as the newest feature update to this Rust-based re-implementation of GNU Coreutils that is used by Ubuntu Linux and other platforms. With Rust Coreutils there are more performance improvements over the prior release: basenc base58 about 35x, cut +23%, date +22%, join +20%, and various other minor performance optimizations. Rust Coreutils 0.13 also spent more time working on remaining GNU Coreutils compatibility issues from their test suite. Rust Coreutils is now passing 95.26% of the GNU Test Suite, up 0.9% from the prior release.

items.summary: They started the year crowned the 2026 Serpentine Pavilion architects and are ending it as trailblazer Frida Escobedo 's pick for the practitioners who will shape the next two decades. items.title: "All over the world, buildings designed to be explored in 3D are subject to restrictions"
items.summary: Controversy over visitors having to pay to access the walkable roof at the new Shanghai Grand Opera House brings into focus the need for architects to be realistic about how buildings operate, writes Aaron Betksy. The beauty of many recent Chinese buildings is that they are also landscapes. You can walk up to them, around them, and through them, but also over them. Ma Yansong 's buildings are often hills that you are invited to climb: the new Shenzhen Bay Cultural Center is a case in point, as is the Quzhou Sports Center, which actually is five different scalable hills, but his oldest major building, the Harbin Opera House of 2015, also offers a path over the auditorium.

items.title: 7 Open Source Speech to Text Tools for Linux (Local AI Dictation)
items.summary: Typing is a fine way to write and a slow way to catch a thought. The most ground-breaking ideas show up while your hands are busy with a soldering iron, a sleeping cat, or a half-eaten taco. Voice input apps overcome that problem because you talk, and it turns your speech into text. Most of the apps in this list are open source, run on Linux, and drop the text into whichever window has focus. That could be a browser tab, a terminal window, or a notes app. Because most of them can run the speech recognition locally on the machine, nothing you say gets sent anywhere.

items.title: XXRI-OS explores the lowest end of the Linux desktop
items.summary: New Linux distros seem to appear daily, but far too few distinguish themselves by being smaller and simpler. XXRI OS is a fairly new desktop Linux distro. It has a snazzy-looking website, complete with an amusing URL, and along similar lines, its GitHub page has a very heavily formatted README. Nonetheless, this is not another over-complex opinionated slopfest of an OS with built-in AI, bizarre keystrokes, and several proprietary components. It's almost the reverse. The main download is just 287.4 MB, and that's the full distro, not a minimalist installer that fetches most of the OS over your internet connection.

items.title: Ancient Cemetery Discovered in Northern Egypt
items.summary: MENOUFIYA GOVERNORATE, EGYPT— Ahram Online reports that a cemetery has been discovered within the ancient city of Teranothis at northern Egypt’s Tell Atrib Abu Bello archaeological site. The city was located near an entrance to the Wadi El-Natrun, a source of the mineral natron that was used in the mummification process. The burials have been dated to the Late Period (712–332 B.C. ) and the Ptolemaic era (304–30 B.C. ), while the tombs range from stone, pottery, and wooden coffins to vaulted structures made of mudbrick.

items.title: FAA Proposes Requiring Electronic Payments for Fees and Penalties
items.summary: The FAA is proposing to eliminate paper payment options for a range of aviation-related fees and civil penalties, bringing its regulations in line with the agency’s existing electronic payment practices. items.title: Inside Chandler's final push to build its own ambulance service as crews train for January launch
items.summary: At Chandler's Public Safety Training Center, the countdown is on. On January 14, seven ambulances with Chandler crews go into service. Four others will be on reserve. "This has been over two decades in the making that we have be wanting to make this a reality and it's imminent, it's here," said Avery Armstrong, battalion chief with the Chandler Fire Department. Chandler has hired outside companies to run its ambulances since 2002, five different companies. items.title: Archaeologists Uncover Medieval Nubia’s Largest Cathedral

The discoveries shed new light on the architectural achievements of the Christian Kingdom of Makuria. A Sudanese-Polish archaeological expedition working at Old Dongola has revealed further sections of the Great Church of Jesus, described in medieval Arabic sources as the largest and wealthiest church in Nubia.

items.summary: A forthcoming documentary spotlights the life and work of luminary artist Jean-Michel Basquiat (1960-1988). The company had recently completed its acquisition of the Big River Steel mill in Osceola, Arkansas. The goal of the expansion: Replicate the success of Big River Steel, which supplies the automotive, construction, and renewable-energy industries and can produce over 3 million tons of steel annually. After an exhaustive search, the company realized there was no reason to look beyond Northeast Arkansas. ​ “ We went to 48 states and narrowed the site selection down to 20, 10, five, and then three,” said Dan Brown, U.

items.title: Anthropic defies the odds, holding record IPO despite ‘massively disruptive’ market
items.summary: The moment felt impossible. Between Jensen Huang's shocking exit from chip giant Nvidia, voters' rebuke of artificial intelligence in this month's midterm elections, and rising interest rates that threatened to stymie plans for a multitrillion-dollar infrastructure buildout, there seemed to be no way Anthropic could carry out an initial public offering. Anthropic's response? Let's go! "Very few companies would've attempted it in this environment," said Byron Deeter, a partner at Bessemer Venture Partners, which counts Anthropic as its biggest investment ever, in an interview.

items.title: US lawmakers target Airbus contracts over China ties
items.summary: As US President Donald Trump wrapped up summit talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping, US lawmakers urged the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) to refuse certification of Chinese-made aircraft and called for stripping US government contracts from aerospace companies that continue investing in China. The House Select Committee on China argues that Western aerospace partnerships have helped China strengthen its military, according to a congressional report published on November 19, 2026. Airbus is among the companies targeted by the proposed contract restrictions.

items.title: A brain region known for listening helps us speak
items.summary: This is a human-written story voiced by AI. Got feedback? Take our survey. (See our AI policy here.) WASHINGTON — A part of the brain famous for listening is important for talking, too. Data collected from people as they listen and try to talk show that this brain region, a small spot inside a larger area called Wernicke’s area, has a more expansive job than researchers thought when it comes to communicating. The results may help efforts to restore people’s voices. The results presented November 15 at the annual meeting of the Society for Neuroscience and published November 19 in Science.

items.title: GTA 6 drives spike in download demand, as estimated sales top $2.3bn
items.summary: Grand Theft Auto 6 is estimated to be the biggest entertainment launch in history after the blockbuster video game debuted on Thursday, following a 13-year wait. Internet infrastructure firm Cloudflare said PS5 downloads in the UK peaked at 8.6 times normal levels around its launch. New Zealand, where GTA 6 was first available, saw a 14.8-fold spike four hours before, suggesting some players switched regions for early access. Pre-orders and first-day sales totalled more than 24.5 million units, making about $2.36bn (Â£1.8bn), according to analytics site Sensor Tower.

items.title: ‘We’re Still Here’ Celebrates Remarkable Quilts by 15 Contemporary Black Artists
items.summary: In the wee hours of a busy Saturday morning, on June 28, 1969, police raided The Stonewall Inn in Manhattan’s Greenwich Village, a renowned hangout for the LGBTQ+ community. During the 1950s and 1960s, few businesses openly welcomed gay people, and the legal system was against them—even two consenting adults in the privacy of their own home could face years in prison or a psychiatric institution if convicted of the crime of sodomy. Bar raids were common, but this one was particularly fraught due to the volume of people, and police quickly lost control.

items.title: "You’re right"—LLMs will get climate info wrong if you ask
items.summary: Many studies over the years have examined how people encounter climate science information. Some focused on the top results that Google surfaced (back when Google was still in the business of serving links), while others examined social media content or newspaper and TV news coverage. With large language models (LLMs) now forming a share of the public information diet, it's worth looking at how they handle climate change. But there’s no direct way for researchers to look at the information people have seen.

items.title: united artists for climate calls for art and culture to take stronger role in climate action at COP31
items.summary: artists call for culture in climate policy at COP31 For its second edition, United Artists for Climate organizes a collective international campaign inviting artists to share their work, creative practices, and environmental initiatives through Instagram. The contributions highlight different ways of engaging with ecological issues, from collaborations with local communities and more responsible approaches to artistic production to new perspectives on humanity’s relationship with the natural world.

items.title: Sticky Miso Chicken and More Recipes We Made This Week
items.summary: It’s no secret that Bon Appétit editors cook a lot for work. So it should come as no surprise that we cook a lot during our off hours too. Here are the recipes we’re whipping up this month to get dinner on the table, entertain our friends, satisfy a sweet tooth, use up leftovers, and everything in between. For even more staff favorites, click here. November 20 Apple picking → snacking cake My husband and I recently took our 3-year-old daughter apple picking. As expected at the tail end of the season, the only apples left were Granny Smith.

items.title: The U.K. and EU hold a rare summit to strengthen ties
items.summary: BRUSSELS — A decade after the people of Britain voted to leave the European Union, top EU officials are meeting with Prime Minister Andy Burnham on Friday, looking to mend more fences, and just perhaps, to pave the way for them to get back together. Burnham has described the rare EU-U.K. summit — only the second since Britain became the first country to leave the world's biggest trading bloc — as a step toward undoing a decade of damage caused by the divorce. "The Brexit we were given has not worked.

items.title: Wake-on-LAN solved my NAS power problem, and it sleeps until I call it
items.summary: NAS, or Network Attached Storage, is a great way to build your own media storage, back up your precious memories or serve as a hub for your smart home automations. Whatever your use case, it is always a great idea to give it a break, especially if you are not doing something that requires the disks to keep spinning 24/7. The good news is that there is an easy way to set up your NAS to wake up when required and go to sleep when not in use.

items.title: Big Win Sets Up Democrats To Intensify Probe of Trump’s Obamacare Purge
items.summary: A week before the midterm elections, a dozen Democratic senators sent harshly critical letters to 10 health insurance company CEOs. Why, the letters asked, had those insurers cooperated with what they called a “potentially unlawful” Trump administration effort that resulted in the rapid cancellation of coverage for 760,000 Affordable Care Act enrollees in late August? Then came the Democrats’ stunning electoral sweep that, come January, will put them in control of both the House and Senate. The power shift lends new weight to the insurance investigation, led by Oregon Sen.

items.title: As Scandinavian Countries Slowly Converted to Christianity, Crusades Often Took on the Form of Viking Raids
items.summary: In 1107, after the First Crusade, Christians held Jerusalem, and Norway’s King Sigurd set sail to defend the city with 60 ships and around 5,000 men. In northern Spain, Sigurd ended up ransacking the fortress at Compostela, one of Western Europe’s holiest sites. He went on to sack Lisbon, storm Ibiza and Minorca, and then team up with King Baldwin of Jerusalem to conquer the port city of Sidon, in modern-day Lebanon. A grateful Baldwin gave Sigurd a fragment of wood from what he said was Jesus’s cross.

items.title: The Most-Saved Recipes on Bon Appétit This Week
items.summary: Like green lentil soup and pumpkin overnight oats. Which recipes earned their keep this week? A slew of lentil bangers, for starters. Like a very green soup, loaded with spinach and herbs, French green lentils, and chewy rice. Also, a curried red lentil soup with crushed tomatoes and coconut milk that according to one reader, “changed my life.” And with Thanksgiving right around the corner (and a big day of cooking looming), make these easy, breezy pumpkin overnight oats for breakfast. Consider it a delicious insurance policy against becoming a hangry holiday menace.

items.title: The Tech Download: Anthropic charmed Wall Street. But one big uncertainty hangs over the business
items.summary: Anthropic's historic debut on Thursday saw the company defy a wider tech selloff, as investors paid a premium for the stock. The five-year-old company, which raised $81.3 billion as part of the listing, is one of the first opportunities for public markets to value a pure play AI lab. Many see the IPO as a possible savior of the AI trade after a shaky few months, but one big uncertainty hangs over the company's future prospects. "One of Anthropic's biggest challenges will be securing enough compute to support their steep growth trajectory," Gil Luria, D.A.

items.title: Dramatic Waves Crash on Iceland’s Coast in
items.summary: Along the rugged volcanic coast of Iceland’s Reykjanes Peninsula, Vilhelm Gunnarsson captures striking storm surf amid natural contrasts. Dark rocks and beaches send foamy waves into high definition, highlighting the forces that physically shape the artist’s home country. Using black-and-white, an approach inspired by fellow artist Ragnar Axelsson, Gunnarsson emphasizes profound tonal shifts and incredible vistas. Doubling as a press photographer and a member of a local rescue team, Gunnarsson is accustomed to working in a range of conditions.

items.title: US and Iran once practiced diplomacy through archaeology—that legacy need not lie in ruins
items.summary: When a U.S. airstrike struck Tehran's Arg Square on March 2, 2026, Golestan Palace was not the target. But it was close enough.

items.title: Community-Focused Academic Brings AI Tools to Colorado Farmers
items.summary: Many farmers and ranchers in eastern Colorado are curious about artificial intelligence, but they don’t have a local tech-savvy person to show them how to use it. Xue “Alice” Dong has made that her job. Dong, an IEEE senior member, is an extension regional specialist with the Colorado State University Extension, CSU’s outreach arm. She works in Logan County and serves a 10-county farming area in Colorado’s northeast corner. Her job is to turn university research into practical help for the people who live there.

items.title: The Classroom of a Black Cat and a Witch Anime Gets English Dub
items.summary: The series debuted on April 12, and it aired for a continuous two cours (quarters of a year) or a half-year run. The anime aired in the "Agaru Anime" programming block on CBC, TBS and 26 other channels on Sundays at 11:30 p.m. Crunchyroll streamed the anime as it aired. Aoyama kun, Mr. Villain's Day Off ) was in charge of series scripts, and Takayuki Onoda ( Hortensia Saga ) designed the characters.

items.title: Dark energy may originate from known laws of particle physics
items.summary: For nearly three decades, scientists have struggled to explain one of the universe's most enduring mysteries: how a component known as dark energy is driving the accelerating expansion of the cosmos.

items.title: National study highlights flexible approaches to integrating pharmacists in aged care
items.summary: A national study led by researchers from RMIT University and the University of Canberra (UC) has identified practical strategies to support the integration of on-site pharmacists in residential elder care homes across metropolitan, regional, rural and remote Australia.

items.title: Spiraling spins bring coordinated quantum motion to diamond sensors
items.summary: Trapped within diamond's crystal lattice are tiny defects called nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers, where a nitrogen atom sits beside an empty gap where a carbon atom should be. Because of their quantum spins, electrons trapped at these defects behave like tiny magnets, turning diamond into a highly sensitive detector for magnetic fields.

items.title: Now Nginx Has Critical Vulnerabilities
items.summary: nginx is an open source web server and reverse proxy that sits in front of apps and passes traffic to them, and it is one of the most widely used web servers around. That kind of broad implementation is why a set of ten vulnerabilities fixed in nginx 1.30.7 and 1.31.9 are significant; five of them even let attackers run code on a server. The stable branch gets its fix in 1.30.7 and mainline gets it in 1.31.9; both went out yesterday. Plus, most of the five only matter if a specific feature is in use.

items.title: New shows & movies to watch this weekend: ‘The Altruists’ on Netflix + more
items.summary: This week, dozens of new releases are flooding in to all the streaming services. On Netflix, you can catch the buzzy new limited series The Altruists, on Disney+, the latest season of Percy Jackson and the Olympians premieres, and on Paramount+, you can catch the season premiere of Yellowjackets. But these aren’t the only big titles dropping this week; on HBO Max, you can now watch movies like The Roses and Tony, on Hulu, that holiday fave A Christmas Story is now streaming, and starting Friday, you can stream the season finale of The Traitors: New Blood on Peacock.

items.title: Bill Hader Made a Horror Movie and We’ll Finally Get to See It
items.summary: Since the end of his HBO show Barry, some fans may have wondered, “ What’s Bill Hader been up to?” Yes, he voiced The Cat in the Hat, but he also wrote, directed, and is starring in a brand-new original horror movie, and soon we’ll get to see it. The film is called They Know, and it stars Hader and Crystal Lake ‘s Linda Cardellini. It’s about “a divorced dad who becomes increasingly suspicious and paranoid that his ex-wifeâs new mysterious partner is exerting a strange, unsettling influence on their children.”

items.title: Token fraud is here and it’s BAD (YouTube)
items.summary: Token fraud is here and it’s BAD (YouTube) Claire Vo runs ChatPRD, an AI platform that helps product managers "turn an idea into a spec". The product has been live since the GPT-4 era, and Claire has been building it in public for much of that time. In this YouTube video (see also the accompanying Twitter post ) Claire describes the flood of token fraud she has seen from groups abusing the product's free trial, sometimes just to get free AI usage but often to resell tokens or run other commercial enterprises on top of the ChatPRD agent.

items.title: How M.C. Escher’s Art Creates Bizarre Mathematical Worlds
items.summary: Maurits Cornelis Escher didn’t plan on becoming the darling of mathematicians. Born in 1898 in the canal-lined city of Leeuwarden in the Netherlands, Escher struggled with mathematics as a student, once remarking that he “never got a pass mark.” He ended up studying decorative arts and printmaking, and he used his artwork to explore the strange rules of nature that he found operating around him. Source…

items.title: CERN scientists finally find evidence of a particle decay so rare it took 40 years to detect
items.summary: Scientists at CERN have found the first evidence of an incredibly rare particle decay after more than 40 years of searching, detecting a process expected to occur just once in every 10 billion beauty particles. The breakthrough could help physicists explore a mysterious microscopic realm where unknown particles and forces may be hiding.

items.title: Scientists turn Moon dust into LEGO-like bricks for future lunar bases
items.summary: Scientists have found a way to 3D-print Moon dust into LEGO-like bricks, raising the possibility of building lunar bases using materials already on the Moon. The experimental blocks still need to be strengthened, but the technology could transform how humans construct permanent settlements beyond Earth.

items.title: Space travel changes the brain's immune cells, but not behavior
items.summary: For those of us on Earth's surface, we reach for sunscreen when we want protection from the sun's radiation. That is because there are other "rays" that the atmosphere and the Earth's magnetic field keep out, like galactic cosmic radiation. Galactic cosmic rays are highly energetic particles found in space.

items.title: Molecular glues: Unlocking new targets in cancer
items.summary: The human genome encodes several hundred E3 ligases—the enzymes that decide which proteins a cell destroys. Drug developers have so far harnessed a small number of them. In a new review in Molecular Cell, researchers at Karolinska Institutet and the University of Verona argue that the rest of these E3 ligases are where the next generation of cancer drugs will be found.

items.title: This simple habit is linked to a 33% lower risk of Alzheimer's
items.summary: Reading for pleasure may have surprisingly powerful benefits for the brain, with studies linking it to better memory, reduced stress, improved mental health, and a lower risk of dementia. Researchers highlight findings that just five minutes of fiction can reduce stress by up to 20%, while reading has also been associated with a 33% lower risk of Alzheimer's disease.

items.title: Deep Rock Galactic Season 7 puts a gravitational twist on the chaotic co-op game, and you can try it right now
items.summary: Rouse a chorus of 'Rock and Stone,' because Deep Rock Galactic Season 7 has just been revealed in full by developer Ghost Ship Games, and there are plenty of reasons to dive back into one of Steam's most gleeful co-op games. The gravity-twisting update will force you to deal with unusual conditions as you attempt…

items.title: Brutal Game Of Thrones Replacement From Best-Selling Fantasy Author Arrives In 2027
items.summary: It's not looking great for Game of Thrones fans in terms of George R.R. Martin's Winds of Winter, with over 15 years since the last installment in A Song of Ice and Fire and no promising updates on a release window to date. Although Martin continues working on the sixth novel, finishing the seven-book saga feels less likely with every passing year. Barring a miracle, HBO's divisive Game of Thrones finale may be the closest fans ever get to a proper ending, even if the books do eventually head somewhere completely different.

items.title: Study reveals data centers’ long-distance damage to air quality
items.summary: The rapid expansion of data centers for artificial intelligence causes negative health and air quality impacts in regions far from where the brick-and-mortar facilities are located, according to a new study by MIT researchers. The team estimates that additional air pollution from the electricity demands of data centers in 2023 resulted in about 650 premature deaths across the United States. Some Midwestern states had among the highest estimated rates of premature deaths per capita attributable to data centers, even though much of the data center electricity demand was concentrated in Virginia and Texas.

items.title: US reacts cautiously to Myanmar genocide ruling as EU praises ‘critical’ role of UN’s top court
items.summary: Reactions to ICJ ruling underline global divisions over court with China raising concerns about judicial overreach The US has greeted with caution the world’s highest court’s ruling that Myanmar committed genocide against its Rohingya minority, while China has raised concerns of judicial overreach. Reactions to Thursday’s historic ruling underlined deep international division over the role of the court and similar institutions. The international court of justice (ICJ) had never previously found a state responsible for genocide and the decision could set a precedent for future genocide claims, notably a case against Israel.

items.title: Arizona MMR vaccination rates among lowest in the nation and still falling
items.summary: PHOENIX Arizona's measles vaccination rates are declining and rank among the lowest in the country, according to an ABC15 data analysis. Arizona's MMR vaccination rate for kindergartners last school year was 87.4%. The herd immunity threshold for measles is 95%, putting Arizona 7 percentage points below that benchmark and the gap is growing. Fifteen years ago, vaccination rates in Arizona were just above 95%. They have fallen nearly every year since, with the exception of 2020 and 2025. During that same period, the personal and medical exemption rate for kindergartners grew from 5% to over 10%.

items.title: Why a Computer Scientist Thinks Superintelligence Won’t Happen
items.summary: Many people were caught off guard this past summer when employees of one of the world’s leading AI companies began casually debating whether their products would lead to human extinction. It started when Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon announced his resignation, warning that his employer and OpenAI were “racing straight to self-improving superintelligence and gambling with our lives.” Evan Hubinger, Anthropic’s head of alignment science, replied, “Jacob is correct here—we really do earnestly believe AI could kill all humans!”

items.title: Τhe Untold History of Brewing Beer From Stone Age Jars to Microorganisms
items.summary: Imagine you are out with friends and you decide to try a new beer. The next thing you know, you are waking up in the emergency room. Though this likely wouldn’t happen today, over ten millennia, people have stared down the Grim Reaper just for the delicious taste of a good buzz. In its most simplistic form, beer includes a handful of basic ingredients: water, barley, yeast, and hops. What could possibly go wrong with this basic recipe? Humans have been making beer for more than 10,000 years, and getting the recipe right has not always been easy.

items.title: Debian Forms New Team to Improve Gaming Hardware Support
items.summary: Debian has announced the creation of a new Gaming Hardware Team whose remit will be to improve Debian’s compatibility with handheld gaming PCs, emulation devices and home consoles. The aim is to make Debian a more viable option for gaming hardware, an area currently dominated by a number of specialist Linux distros. The announcement came from Debian maintainer Aryan Karamtoth, who pointed to the massive strides that Linux gaming has made over the last few years, particularly since the launch of Valve’s Steam Deck.

items.title: Changes in the heart's electrical signals anticipate the most severe arrhythmias in heart failure patients
items.summary: The heart gives warning signs. It does so through small electrical variations—signals so subtle that until now they have gone unnoticed among the millions of data points generated by implantable defibrillators. Today, thanks to remote analysis of the cardiac signal, these whispers can become an early warning.

items.title: How Inanna, Sumer’s Goddess of Love and War, Legitimized Its Kings
items.summary: Ancient Sumer is known as humanity’s earliest civilization (c. 4500-1900 BC). Its religion was ruled by a complex pantheon of principal gods. Perhaps the most renowned of these was Inanna, the goddess of love and war, who also played an interesting role in royal ideology and ideas of ascension and deification. Inanna was one of ancient Sumer’s most powerful deities, carrying the title of Queen of Heaven. Inanna Was Sumer’s Goddess of Love and War and Patron of Uruk Inanna was the goddess of love and war.

items.title: Kitty 0.51 Terminal Emulator Adds Docked Windows, New Shaders
items.summary: Kitty, the GPU-accelerated, cross-platform terminal emulator, has released version 0.51, featuring OS-level docked windows, new custom shader effects, improved container support, and security fixes. The update arrives two weeks after version 0.50, which introduced initial docked-window functionality. The main improvement is an expanded set of docking options. Users can attach terminal windows directly to the edge of an OS window, below the tab bar, using the new launch --type=os-window-dock option.

items.title: Three 'e-waste' Nvidia V100s hit 100 tokens per second on Qwen 3.6 35B in a $1,042 homelab rig
items.summary: A homelab builder benchmarked three used Nvidia V100s on Qwen 3.6 35B, achieving about 100 tokens per second in a custom setup costing $1,042 with just “e-waste” GPUs. The smaller, dense Qwen 3.6 27B manages about 24 tokens per second on the same platform, and the V100s use about half the energy of the same number of P100s for a given job. The blog post, “Scaling ‘E-Waste’: LLMs on Multiple Decommissioned GPUs,” compares nine different builds — one to three K80s, P100s, or V100-16GB cards — on a single Supermicro dual-Xeon board.

items.title: For better mental health, how often you exercise may matter more than how hard
items.summary: A study of more than 10,000 college students found that exercising regularly may be more important for mental health than pushing yourself through intense or lengthy workouts. Students who exercised less frequently were more likely to experience depression and anxiety a year later, suggesting that consistency could be a key ingredient in protecting mental well-being.

items.title: when bees and humans make art together
items.summary: Ava Roth and the art of Kintsu-Bee One of Ava Roth’s most valuable collaborators is not human. In fact, it’s the bees. In her series, Kintsu-Bee, she places broken ceramics into a hive of bees who, through the formation of honeycombs, create a new bond between the cracked pieces. The method is named after the Japanese repair method, kintsugi, which uses lacquer and gold leaf to create a shining new seam in broken dishware, turning what was once considered waste into a valuable new form. From this, Roth’s work expands beyond cups and plates.

items.title: Emails reveal how Trump allies pushed pardons for election deniers
items.summary: Former Trump lawyer urged justice department officials to seek pardons for those falsely claiming he won the 2020 presidential election in their states In the fall of 2025, Cleta Mitchell, a key lawyer in Donald Trump’s efforts to overturn the 2020 presidential election, contacted a justice department official with an urgent request. Criminal cases against people who signed certificates falsely claiming that Trump won the presidential election in their state – known widely as fake electors – were pending in Georgia, Michigan, Arizona, Nevada and Wisconsin.

items.title: ‘I agree with the president’: incoming senator Abdul El-Sayed seeks to help Trump end military aid to Israel
items.summary: Michigan senator-elect also secured a meeting with JD Vance, who called him a ‘terrible evil’ in lead-up to election The incoming US senator Abdul El-Sayed of Michigan said that he and Donald Trump were in agreement about ending foreign military aid to Israel – and he hopes to find more common ground with the US president when he takes office. “I agree with the president – I can’t believe I’m saying that – that we need to end foreign military aid that is unconditional to Israel, as well as Egypt and Saudi Arabia and Pakistan,” the senator-elect said.

items.title: Study Pushes Back Cultivation of Millet in Bronze Age Poland
items.summary: POZNAŃ, POLAND—Millet was grown and consumed in Poland around 1590 B.C., or about 100 years earlier than previously thought, Science in Poland reports. Przemysław Makarowicz of Adam Mickiewicz University and his colleagues analyzed the isotopes in the teeth and bones of more than 190 individuals whose remains were recovered at archaeological sites in Poland and dated to between 2200 and 1000 B.C. The study suggests that millet, which is drought-resistant and grows quickly, was introduced gradually into the diet and became more important over time.

items.title: GRRIZ’s moiré sculpture set atop paris parking entrance moves only when people walk past it
items.summary: GRRIZ INSTALLS MOIRÉ SCULPTURE ATOP PARKING ENTRANCE IN PARIS Installed on the parvis de la Grande Arche at Paris La Défense, CROMAWALTZ is a permanent, unpowered sculpture by Italian-French studio GRRIZ. Commissioned by Q-Park for Paris La Défense and curated by Archibald Verney-Carron (Art Entreprise), the project marks the studio’s first permanent installation in France. Crowned atop the cylindrical granite entrance volume of the Les 4 Temps P2 parking garage, the facade wraps the infrastructure in an undulating profile without motors or electricity.

items.title: Proton’s Lumo AI chatbot is now available on Linux desktops
items.summary: Proton has released desktop apps for its Lumo AI chatbot on all major desktop OSes, including Linux. Lumo is the Swiss privacy company’s own AI assistant, introduced last year and available to use on line. It offers the same sort of features as other generative AI chatbots, including text and image generation, memory, web searching and editable canvases. It runs on ‘open models’, touts better privacy safeguards and encrypts users’ chat history. It’s free to use (with limits) on a free Proton account.

items.title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged
items.summary: In Uganda's northern Karamoja region, Elijah Lobur and his family now eat just one meal a day. A severe drought that began in April has destroyed crops, while food brought in from elsewhere has become increasingly unaffordable. "Seven months without rain has brought us to this point where we now live in hunger," the 44-year-old farmer, who lives with his grandmother, wife and five children, told the BBC. "Even some of the wild plants that we used to eat have withered and dried up." Local officials say more than 90% of crops have failed in the region, where agriculture is largely rain-fed.

items.title: Theorizer comes to Asta
items.summary: Theorizer in Asta connects scientific literature to proposed explanations that researchers can examine and test.

items.title: Celebrating the Eater Awards Winners With a Party in NYC
items.summary: What a night. On Sunday, November 15, the winners of the 2026 Eater Awards, presented by Capital One, celebrated together at Nine Orchard in NYC. More than 200 chefs, restaurateurs, bartenders, and friends of Eater — many of whom traveled across the country to be there — partook in live portraiture, custom engraving, and, of course, plenty of food and drink. Now in its 17th year, the Eater Awards recognize the year’s best new restaurants, bakeries, bars, dishes, and chefs in markets across the U.S..

items.title: Unexpected Safety Incident Grounds British Airways Boeing 777 After Slide Deployment
items.summary: COLOMBO – A British Airways (BA) Boeing 777-200ER was forced out of service in Sri Lanka after an emergency evacuation slide unexpectedly deployed during pre-departure preparations, disrupting travel plans and grounding a scheduled flight to the United Kingdom. The incident occurred at Bandaranaike International Airport in Colombo as the aircraft was being prepared for Flight BA2044 to London Gatwick. While no injuries were reported, the unexpected deployment brought ground operations around the aircraft to an immediate halt and prevented the flight from departing as scheduled.

items.title: A doctor’s guide to surviving — and enjoying — holiday feasting while on GLP-1 medication
items.summary: Thanksgiving and the winter holidays bring celebration, connection and plenty of opportunities to come together with family and friends. But the holiday season also brings something else: more food-centered gatherings, larger portions and richer foods than most people typically eat throughout the year. Think whipped sweet potatoes, mac and cheese, decadent side dishes and an abundance of desserts. For people taking GLP-1 medications for diabetes management, weight loss or other medical reasons, these celebrations can present unique challenges.

items.title: Ubisoft stock drops 11% as GTA VI competition dims its holiday forecast
items.summary: Ubisoft forecast net bookings of about €250 million ($280 million) for the quarter ending in December, and its stock fell about 11% in Paris trading on Friday. The company said on Thursday that the outlook reflects a crowded holiday season. Ubisoft confirmed its full-year targets: net bookings down by a high single-digit percentage, a high single-digit negative non-IFRS operating margin and free cash flow consumption of no more than €500 million ($560 million). The €250 million forecast is a 26% decline from €338 million a year earlier, according to Bloomberg.

items.summary: Surprisingly mellow illustrations of war and myth from a book of advice for young noblemen.

items.title: China issues Mount Fuji warning as family of missing climber offers reward
items.summary: The Chinese embassy in Japan has warned its citizens against off-season ascents of Mount Fuji amid concerns that the hefty reward offered by a missing hiker's family could encourage more reckless climbing. Chen Jie, 25, vanished on 8 November on the mountain. His family is offering 500,000 yuan ($75,000; Â£57,300) to anyone who finds him alive, and 100,000 yuan to anyone who recovers his body, say Chinese and Japanese media reports. Strong winds and blizzards pose serious risks during the closed season, especially as shelter and first-aid centres are not operational, the embassy said on Tuesday.

items.title: The Tucson Restaurant Turning Cactus Into Fine Dining
items.summary: Traipsing through Tucson Mountain Park, a Midwestern blow-in might not identify much to eat. Plants armed with burs, barbs, and spines all but scream “do not touch.” For chef Aaron Lopez and June Chee, however, this prickly, dusty landscape stocks a pantry of possibility. The married co-owners of Ursa see the Arizona desert as a rich ground for foraging. Gray, tangled brittlebush, which the average Tucsonan walks or drives by almost daily, can be pressure-cooked, caramelized until black, and baked into cake.

items.title: The College Kids Who Drove a Duck Across the Americas
items.summary: The DUKW was designed for war. The gray metal vehicle had six wheels, a rudder, and a propeller, an unlikely cross between a Jimmy deuce-and-a-half—as the standard GMC military truck was known—and a bulky metal scow. Between 1942 and 1945, more than 21,000 DUKWs came off the assembly lines in Michigan and Missouri. It long predates DOGE. In fact it goes back decades. And Musk literally warned about this specific network failing last year.

items.title: Life with an Ordinary Guy Who Reincarnated into a Total Fantasy Knockout Manga Ends With 20th Volume
items.summary: Nerdy office worker Hinata has once again blundered at a singles mixer, no thanks to his hunky best friend, Jinguji, who's always by his side. While he's grumbling about it on the way home, a naked goddess appears out of nowhere and sends the two friends to another world--while also turning Hinata into a hot young woman! To get back Hinata's original body, Hinata and Jinguji set off on a journey to defeat the demon king, even if Hinata's new feminine form is giving them...unexpected feelings. Can they save this fantasy world before their lifelong bromance becomes a romance?

items.title: Apple TV’s 6-Episode Fantasy Series Is a Masterclass in Imaginative Worldbuilding
items.summary: Over the past few years, Apple TV has slowly been building a hefty catalog of endearing dramas in addition to its beloved sci-fi and crime thrillers. From the Jason Sudeikis -led Ted Lasso to the underseen drama Trying and, of course, Jason Segel 's Shrinking, the streaming platform has become a go-to for heartwarming and perhaps even tear-jerking stories. Among them is Small Prophets, an original BBC production which first landed on Apple TV on October 7, 2026.

items.title: Nations League quarterfinal draw: Spain face France, England play Norway
items.summary: World champions Spain will face France while England will play Norway in the quarterfinals of the UEFA Nations League after the draw took place on Friday. Spain beat France 2-0 in the semifinals of the World Cup in the United States in July on the way to winning the trophy. They also defeated Les Bleus 5-4 in the semifinals of the last edition of the Nations League last year. The quarterfinals will be played over two legs in late March with Spain at home first after coming second in Group A3 while France topped Group A1.

items.title: Mouldy, infested housing for vulnerable people sold as ethical investments abroad
items.summary: "This building is hell on Earth," says Phil, describing the black mould and rats at Castleview House, the block of flats in Runcorn, Cheshire, where he lives. The estate agent's marketing material said the flat was a government-funded source of income for investors, where tenants were taken care of and the property was in excellent condition. A Czech investor bought it last year for Â£163,150, more than double the Â£75,000 cost of similar apartments in the block. The BBC has found more than 40 companies marketing similar properties to individuals in the UK and abroad, as businesses seek to profit from a government system intended to provide housing and support for vulnerable people.

items.title: What Makes Notre-Dame Cathedral a Masterpiece of Gothic Architecture
items.summary: Most of us remember where we were when we heard that Notre-Dame had burned down. And even upon learning that the most famous of all French cathedrals had been badly damaged rather than completely destroyed, it still felt as if something irreplaceable had been lost. It made no difference whether we’d actually been to the place, as I hadn’t at the time. When I did finally make it to Paris four years later, Notre-Dame’s restoration was still underway, and construction walls prevented anyone from seeing much of anything at ground level, let alone entering.

items.title: ‘GTA VI’ Has a Full-Blown Bigfoot Horror Mystery Hidden in Its Swamps
items.summary: He really does exist. As we reported earlier this morning, Rockstar has just released the long-awaited GTA VI, and fans are already discovering a ton of horror-related easter eggs, such as Dexter’s apartment building. Now, we’ve also learned that Bigfoot is roaming the map…and he has a full-blown mystery storyline. The Big Lead has posted a full walkthrough of how to find Bigfoot in GTA VI, known in the game as Mister Mangrove, AKA Skunk Ape, Leonida’s version of Bigfoot. You might be asking yourself, why is Bigfoot in Florida, to which I would say, well, maybe he’s the long-lost cousin of Florida Man (men.

items.summary: Google LLC is releasing a new version of its Gemini artificial intelligence assistant that is better at performing multistep tasks. Josh Woodward, the vice president responsible for the Gemini app, detailed the update in a Tuesday blog post. The AI assistant has two modes that are accessible through separate interface tabs. The first, Chat, generates…

items.title: 'A Pen, Handcuffs, and a Common-Law Marriage' TV Anime Reveals Theme Song Artists, More Cast, January 9 Debut in Video
items.summary: King Amusement Creative revealed the main promotional video on Friday for the television anime of storywriter Shinichi Sawaragi and artist Tanku Gasuyama 's A Pen, Handcuffs, and a Common-Law Marriage ( Pen to Wappa to Jijitsu Kon ) manga that reveals the anime's opening and ending theme song artists, more cast members, and January 9 debut. The company also revealed a key visual for the anime. The anime will debut on January 9 at 25:00 (effectively January 10 at 1:00 a.m.) on Tokyo MX and BS11. Inori Minase performs the opening theme song “Mikaiketsu de, Romance de” (Unsolved and Romantic), and saeco performs the ending theme song “Message.”

items.title: Simple Lab Test May Predict Recurrence Risk in Most Common Type of Breast Cancer
items.summary: Higher levels of circulating eosinophils had a significant association with improved recurrence-free survival (RFS) and distant metastasis-free survival (DMFS) in hormone receptor (HR)-positive breast cancer, a large retrospective analysis showed.With an eosinophil cutoff of 0.08 × 109/L, patients with eosinophil counts above the cutoff had significantly better RFS (P=0.001) and DMFS (P=0.002). Higher levels of circulating eosinophils remained an independent predictor of improved outcomes in multivariable-adjusted statistical models.

items.title: Major Fantasy Reboot Confirms Season 2 Return After 3 Years With New Look
items.summary: Rebooted adaptations of classic anime franchises have become increasingly popular in recent years, with seasonal lineups featuring star-studded titles making massive comebacks like Science Saru’s modernized spin on Ghost in the Shell and TMS Entertainment’s reboot of Fruits Basket, both of which promised to deliver stories that were more faithful retellings of their respective source materials. This trend is only set to continue with the long-awaited announcement that Studio Passione’s reboot of Isuna Hakekura’s original series Spice and Wolf will be getting a second season.

items.summary: It tastes like dessert. The Kitchn: I Finally Found a Protein Bar I Actually Look Forward to Eating (It Tastes Like Dessert!).

items.title: Blood Test May Detect CTE During Life, Study Shows
items.summary: Detecting chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE) in living patients may soon be possible, according to preliminary data from a case series.CTE, a neurodegenerative disease associated with repetitive head impacts from contact sports, currently can be diagnosed only at autopsy.In a study of 21 former American football players who had donated their brains, however, blood levels of endogenously cleaved microtubule-binding region tau (eMTBR-tau) were higher in CTE-positive participants than in CTE-negative participants (β=1.61, 95% CI 0.51-2.70), reported Annalise Miner, a PhD candidate working on research under Michael Alosco, PhD, of Boston University, at the Clinical Trials on Alzheimer's…

items.title: I Asked 3 Chefs the Best Way to Make Flaky Pie Crust — They All Agreed on This Golden Rule
items.summary: Thanksgiving is right around the corner, which means it is peak pie time. This time of year I’m partial to sweet potato pie, but I’ll happily take pecan pie or Dutch apple pie too. Whether you’re making a classic or trying something new and experimental, one thing you can’t get wrong is the crust.

items.title: ‘Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2’ Writer Dives Into Anime Aftermath Spoilers
items.summary: We’re just shy of a month out from CD Projekt Red and studio Trigger’s follow-up anime video game adaptation Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2, and honestly, we’re still reeling from the emotional damage from our second run through the world of Cyberpunk 2077. If you’re like us, you need to chat with someone to debrief on all the bedlam the Netflix series had to offer. So we did, through a spoiler-filled conversation picking up the pieces with showrunner and writer Bartosz Sztybor. Isaiah Colbert, io9: One of the most intriguing revelations in the season is the connection between David Martinez and D.

items.title: I Never Use My Slow Cooker for Dinner on Thanksgiving, I Save It For This Instead
items.summary: Thanksgiving food gets all the glory, but I think the drinks deserve some love, too. While I love a glass of fizzy red, or a 2-ingredient spritz with my turkey and stuffing, I’m also a sucker for a warm cocktail. Who doesn’t love a nice hot toddy or a mug of warm, spiced wine with pie at the end of the feast? All of that said, I don’t have the time or energy to make individual warm cocktails for every guest. That’s what my slow cooker is for.

items.title: How Klafs Is Rethinking the Sauna Through Design
items.summary: The sauna is Finnish. The company reimagining it for contemporary homes and spas is German. Klafs, based in Schwäbisch Hall, Germany, sees no contradiction. Its designers approach the centuries-old ritual through engineering, experimenting with heat, air, and materials. As wellness culture expands, the language surrounding its rituals has become increasingly fluid. In my own friend group, “banya” has become nearly shorthand for any spa visit, though it refers specifically to the Russian-style bathhouse.

items.title: The Next Horror Film From the ‘Insidious 6’ Director Adds and Subtracts More Cast
items.summary: So much for all our excitement over Parker Posey starring in Sleepover, the next film from Insidious: Out of the Further director Jacob Chase. She’s no longer part of the film. But there’s new reason to get excited for this one, because the cast will now feature Michelle Monaghan (taking over Posey’s role) along with Justin Theroux. Deadline shared news of the casting, which brings two veteran actors to the film, though Theroux is probably better-known to horror fans. His many genre movie credits include Beetlejuice Beetlejuice and Mulholland Drive; on the small screen, he’s been seen in Fallout and The Leftovers, among many others.

items.title: The best things in open source are built together
items.summary: In 2026, public contributions on GitHub soared to 2.5 billion, more than double last year’s total of 1.12 billion. It goes to show how open source remains a powerful mechanism for developers to build, share, and grow communities. Open source is how I began my GitHub journey. I contributed to Processing Foundation by adding alt-text to images on the p5.js website. This was the first time I felt included in a software development space as someone with a background in traditional fine arts and design.

items.title: France deploys nuclear-capable Rafales to Sweden for first deterrence drill
items.summary: Rafale fighters from the French Strategic Air Forces (FAS) were deployed to Sweden from November 16 to 18, 2026, as part of Exercise Excalibur, the first joint exercise under the two countries’ forward deterrence framework, the Swedish Armed Forces announced on November 19, 2026. The French aircraft operated alongside Swedish Air Force Gripen fighters in northern Sweden, supported by an Airbus A330 MRTT tanker, according to a separate statement from the French Ministry of the Armed Forces. The exercise aimed to improve interoperability between the two air forces and demonstrate their ability to collaborate.

items.title: US firms seek new 250-mile speed lane for supersonic-hypersonic flight tests
items.summary: A group of US companies are looking to establish a new 250-mile speed corridor between Texas and New Mexico as a supersonic and hypersonic flight test facility. On November 18, 2026, the four members, which includes two FAA -licensed spaceports, signed a letter of intent (LOI) to “jointly define, advocate for, and develop a dedicated high-speed flight test corridor”. Midland Development Corporation, Midland International Air & Space Port, the New Mexico Spaceport Authority, operator of Spaceport America, and Starfighters Space said the “proposal comes as federal regulators consider easing overland supersonic flight restrictions and expanding US space launch capacity”.

items.title: Traumatized teens sue school, cops after Doritos bag triggers AI gun alert
items.summary: In October 2025, four Black high school students were sharing Cool Ranch Doritos after football practice, winding down and waiting for their rides home. It was then, in the lull of a moment any teen with after-school activities knows well, that the school’s AI gun detection system suddenly flagged one teen holding a bag of chips as a potential gunman. Within two minutes, Baltimore County Public Schools officials who reviewed security camera footage linked to the alert determined there was no actual threat.

items.title: How exactly did Trump get so rich on crypto? We explain
items.summary: For the last year, Will Ragland and a team of researchers at the Center for American Progress — a left-leaning think tank in Washington, D.C. — have dedicated themselves to counting how much money President Trump and his family have made in his second term. So far, they put the total at nearly $3 billion. More than 2 billion dollars of the earnings come from cryptocurrency ventures. "You could probably combine all of the past presidents' income made during their time in office," Ragland says. "And it wouldn't come close to what we're seeing here."

items.title: Why The Airbus A350-1000 Is The Only Jet That Can Fly Sydney To London Nonstop
items.summary: Qantas is gearing up to launch the world’s longest-ever commercial service between Sydney and London At 9,188 nautical miles (10,573 miles or 17,016 km) and scheduled to exceed 20 hours, the nonstop journey linking the Australian city and English capital will far outdo anything attempted by an airline before. But such an undertaking is no mean feat, and is something that cannot simply be served by any old aircraft.

items.title: Stock Photos of Muscular Men in Odd Places
items.summary: Muscle Plus is a free stock photo site that features Japanese bodybuilders in unusual places and situations. From Tokyo Weekender: There are men declaring their love in the middle of a tea plantation, men frolicking among sunflowers and men who have been abandoned in cardboard boxes, sometimes in the woods, sometimes by the roadside. The last scenario has proved popular enough to warrant an entire category, sute macho, or “abandoned buff guy,” borrowing its premise from the stray kittens left in cardboard boxes by Japanese roadsides.

items.title: Why United Airlines Doesn't Want Its Airbus A320s Anymore
items.summary: Many US airlines are now modernizing their fleet by switching to more efficient and sustainable jets. United is not an exception and is currently accelerating a fleet modernization that will soon make one of its most familiar workhorses, the A320, a rare sight in its livery. But why this jet?

items.summary: AWS has released AWS Emulator, a free, CC0-licensed local stand-in for more than 200 of its services, generated from its public API models and aimed at the test loops of coding agents. items.title: PostgreSQL 19 Released
items.summary: PostgreSQL 19 Released Most years PostgreSQL ships a new release in September, but this year's release came two months later thanks mainly to the flurry of issues that the PostgreSQL team needed to address as part of the ongoing AI-reported vulnerability apocalypse. This release was definitely worth the wait. My favorite new feature is this one: For applications that send reads to standbys, PostgreSQL 19 adds "read-your-writes" consistency with the new WAIT FOR LSN command.

items.title: I Walked Solo Along England’s Rugged South West Coast Path for Three Days
items.summary: I’m standing atop a spit of land jutting out into the English Channel, peering down at a beach accessible only by boat, where a small group of sunbathers lounge on the rocky sand. The view is a welcome excuse to catch my breath before continuing along five more rolling cliffs—400 steep feet up, 400 steep feet down, and repeat. And so, despite my exhausted legs and the blister that’s forming over my right big toe, I decide to imprint this impossibly peaceful scene into my brain to remind myself why I’m doing this trip.

items.title: Our Editors Test Tons of Gear. We’re Still Using These 22 Items Years Later.
items.summary: Our Writers Test Tons of Gear. These Are the 22 Items We’re Still Using. g a snapshot in time — an editor tested a new piece of luggage on a flight or wore a waterproof jacket on a few rainy camping trips. So when you’re someone who writes gear reviews, you have a lot of gear. Some is randomly mailed to you in the hopes you’ll like it and write about it, and there’s plenty we buy, because different types of travel call for different types of gear (and we travel whenever we can). Some gear stays in our closets, some gets donated, and some doesn’t quite live up to the hype, so we don’t write about it at all.

items.title: Electric Aircraft Tests Solid-State Batteries at 17,200 Feet
items.summary: Helios Horizon has completed a series of flight tests using solid-state batteries in its modified Pipistrel Taurus aircraft. According to a Nov. 18 announcement, founder and test pilot Miguel Iturmendi reached 17,200 feet during one flight and used approximately 36% of the aircraft’s battery capacity. The tests were conducted in partnership with the University of North Dakota’s John D. Odegard School of Aerospace Sciences. Three Record Claims The nonprofit organization said the flight exceeded three existing world records for electric aircraft weighing less than 500 kilograms (1,102 pounds).

items.title: Archer, Disney Team on Electric Aircraft Research
items.summary: Archer Aviation and Walt Disney Imagineering R&D announced a research collaboration Nov. 19 focused on potential applications of emerging transportation technology. The companies said they will initially examine technical and passenger-experience concepts. Neither company has identified specific projects, development commitments or a timeline for the research. Marvel-Themed Aircraft Appears in Las Vegas The announcement coincides with the Formula 1 Las Vegas Grand Prix, which runs Nov. 19-21. Archer’s Midnight electric vertical takeoff and landing (eVTOL) aircraft is on display in a special Disney and Marvel Studios Avengers: Doomsday livery.

items.title: Texas County Votes to Close McLean Airport
items.summary: Gray County commissioners in Texas have voted to close McLean/Gray County Airport (2E7), citing limited traffic and deteriorating conditions at the rural airfield. The decision follows a Nov. 2 commissioners court meeting, where officials considered concerns raised by the Texas Department of Transportation’s Aviation Division. The airport’s future was listed on the county’s meeting agenda, and local reporting indicates officials agreed that continued maintenance was no longer practical. Airport Conditions “The McLean Airport has very limited usage,” Precinct 1 Commissioner Logan Hudson told KVII.

items.title: New Ukraine talks including Europe to be held 'soon' — Merz
items.summary: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said on Thursday he believes new talks regarding Russia's invasion of Ukraine with European leaders taking part will occur "soon." "Of course we are prepared to hold talks with Russia, we have always said this. These talks are now set to take place soon," Merz said after a meeting of Ukraine's allies in Berlin. He did not give a concrete date for the next talks, but said Europe's interests would be represented by Germany, France, the UK, Poland and Italy.

items.title: The Amazing Inventions of Ancient Greece: From Plato’s Alarm Clock to Ancient Flamethrowers
items.summary: Pla­to’s water alarm clock is just one of the pieces of advanced ancient Greek tech­nol­o­gy explained in the new video above from Lost in Time, a YouTube chan­nel whose look at ancient Roman tech­nol­o­gy we post­ed here on Open Cul­ture last year. Most of the oth­ers were invent­ed for less gen­tle pur­pos­es: we have a nasty-look­ing flamethrow­er on wheels meant to breach stone fortress­es; a “machine gun” able to fire arrows much more rapid­ly than any bow­man; a nine-sto­ry-tall pro­to-tank ful­ly stocked with cat­a­pults and sol­diers ready to swarm a city; and a gigan­tic claw, designed by no less a mind than Archimedes, able to grab and over­turn invad­ing war­ships.

items.title: The Psychedelic Animated Video for Kraftwerk’s “Autobahn” (1979)
items.summary: Ah, yes, “Autobahn.” From the moment the door slams and the ignition starts, prog rockers and pre-new wavers know a journey is afoot. Though Kraftwerk had already made three albums, and the band members still looked like well-meaning, bookish hippies, 1974’s “Autobahn” is considered Year Zero for the denizens of the Electric Café, the four German robots who made human music with machines. This cel-drawn animation by Roger Mainwood was made in 1979 to promote “Autobahn,” after most of the culture had caught up with the song, and it’s now bopping around pop culture again.

items.title: Airport Hangar Evictions Put on Hold in New Jersey
items.summary: The New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) has agreed to a six-month pause in planned evictions at Aeroflex-Andover Airport (12N) following concerns raised by state lawmakers, local officials and airport tenants. According to local WRNJ Radio, the department will conduct a broader review of the airport’s long-term viability and future operations. The agreement follows months of opposition to the state’s plans to demolish much of the airport’s hangar complex. Tenants received eviction notices requiring them to vacate by Dec.

items.title: The Best Places to Go in Central and South America 2027
items.summary: This is my fourth year leading our guide to the Best Places to Go in Central and South America, and each time I’m in awe of the final result—our list for 2027 is no exception. We’re talking about a region where the Pacific, the Atlantic, and the Caribbean converge; where the Andes reach for the Amazon; and where strings of puffy volcanoes and postcard-worthy islands stud the map like jewels. Within it all there are thriving cities where cultures ancient and modern collide head-on, and small towns that are timeless in a way that feels increasingly rare.

items.title: Finnair Operates All-Male Flight for International Men’s Day
items.summary: VANTAA- Finnair (AY) marked International Men’s Day on November 19, 2026, by operating flight AY1331 with an all-male crew from Helsinki Airport (HEL) to London Heathrow Airport (LHR). The service used an Airbus A350-900. The 10-member crew included two pilots and eight flight attendants. Male employees also handled the flight’s gate operations, highlighting Finnair’s efforts to encourage more men to pursue careers in cabin crew positions. Finnair Highlights Gender Imbalance in Cabin Crew Finnair used its International Men’s Day operation to draw attention to the gender imbalance in the airline industry, particularly within cabin crew departments.

items.title: GA Safety Group Highlights Automation Risks in CFIT Accidents
items.summary: The General Aviation Joint Safety Committee (GAJSC) is warning pilots about the risks of relying too heavily on cockpit automation, noting that autopilot use and declining hand-flying proficiency can contribute to controlled flight into terrain (CFIT) accidents. In a safety briefing published Nov. 16, the committee said advances in situational awareness technology have helped reduce CFIT accidents in general aviation. However, its review found that automation has also emerged as a contributing factor in accidents involving both visual and instrument meteorological conditions, during day and night operations.

items.title: Producing Healthy Code with Artificial Intelligence Costs Fewer Tokens
items.summary: Agentic AI can speed up velocity, but the gains vanish within months as code complexity grows. Healthy code makes AI perform better and costs fewer tokens. Safeguarding means keeping code health high through agentic refactoring, with an MCP supplying code health data, so AI can maintain the code it generates. By Ben Linders…

items.title: A convincing vegan meat alternative needs both taste and texture – here’s how food scientists manufacture them
items.summary: This Thanksgiving, you may sit down to a table laden with mashed potatoes, cranberry sauce, vegetables and a golden-brown turkey. And, if you have any vegetarians or vegans in your family, you may even see a plant-based meat alternative. But how do food scientists make something taste and look similar to turkey entirely from plants? Plant-based meat alternatives have become an increasingly prominent part of the food industry, driven partly by concerns about the sustainability of conventional meat production and the search for additional protein sources.

items.title: New electric comb from China regrew nearly 100% of hair (in mice)
items.summary: A potentially revolutionary electronic comb is generating some pretty hair-raising results. The experimental comb has been used to successfully restore nearly all the hair in bald test subjects. But don’t chuck out that Rogaine just yet. The comb’s users were mice with shaved backs. Though the Detangle comb (named after the 2010 Disney film Tangled ) hasn’t been tested on humans yet, the Chinese scientist behind its development says the eye-grabbing results on our distant genetic cousins suggest it could play a role in the neverending quest to keep those luscious locks just a hair longer.

items.title: Mesa dog trainer and rescue dog face long road to recovery after car crash
items.summary: MESA – When Keylee Harvey rescued Rogue about two years ago, she met a dog who was shut down, lacked confidence and rarely showed interest in playing with toys. But Harvey helped Rogue come out of her shell through training, patience and a lot of time together. The two became inseparable. “She’s beautiful. She’s like no other. I couldn’t imagine my life without her,” Harvey said. What began as a rescue grew into a partnership built around training, play and shared adventures. Rogue became Harvey’s constant companion, joining her on trips and spending nearly every day by her side.

items.title: Steak Marinade Gets Extra Smoky And Flavorful With 3 Underappreciated Ingredients
items.summary: Marinating meat can make a huge difference in its taste and texture, but it's even more important to know which ingredients to add to your marinade. We've already discussed the three ingredients for the simplest steak marinade, but making a uniquely tasty marinade with depth and smokiness will require three ingredients that might not be the first that come to mind: balsamic vinegar, red wine, and liquid smoke. Each can have a profound impact on your steak, and to discuss why these three ingredients are a great choice for a smoky marinade, we spoke with Dagan Lynn, the executive chef at Beef.

items.title: 'Pepper pileup' closes two lanes of busy Florida road
items.summary: Authorities in Florida said two lanes of a busy roadway were temporarily closed when a truck lost 19 pallets of peppers into the roadway.

items.title: Outdoor Research Austera Alpine Down Hoodie Review
items.summary: Bottom Line The Outdoor Research Austera Alpine Down Hoodie delivers substantial warmth for its 16.2-ounce weight and allows good shoulder mobility when reaching overhead. Its lofty 850-fill insulation and Pertex Quantum Diamond Fuse shell make it a useful cold-weather layer, while the two-way zipper and helmet-compatible hood are practical for climbing. We found the shell sheds water in light rain, but that is not a substitute for a waterproof rain layer. The two-way main zipper, helmet-compatible hood, and large internal mesh pockets are useful climbing-oriented details, though our assessment centered on the features and fit rather than a documented high-altitude trip.

items.title: AI agents ask better questions than KPMG accountants in audit trial
items.summary: LONDON, November 18, 2026 — Artificial intelligence has taken another significant step into the world of professional services after KPMG revealed that AI agents examining the accounts of a major UK-listed company sometimes investigated financial issues more deeply and asked better questions than its human audit team. The experiment, conducted by KPMG UK using more than 100 AI agents, marks an important development in the application of artificial intelligence to one of the most labour-intensive areas of the financial services industry.

items.title: 10 Words and Names in the ‘Hunger Games’ Franchise Drawn From Ancient Greece and Rome
items.summary: The Hunger Games franchise is currently in the midst of a massive revival, with two prequel books released in the last six years and the latest movie adaptation coming to theaters on November 20. With author Suzanne Collins expanding what we know about the world of Panem, her Classical inspirations are becoming increasingly obvious. Collins has discussed the origins of The Hunger Games on multiple occasions, explaining that she was channel surfing when the coexistence of reality television and genuine war footage sparked her imagination.

items.summary: A school in Northern Ireland is encouraging pupils not to stay home to play "Grand Theft Auto VI" by offering the chance to win prizes.

items.title: Nurse spends $50,000 on a new car to drive home after US flights grounded
items.summary: A woman splashed out on a $50,000 car so that she could get home during the nationwide air travel stop in the United States, and ended up driving for 27 hours. Back on November 13, travel plans across the United States were plunged into chaos after a nationwide ground stop was put on planes. The stoppage saw 20,000 flights disrupted, leaving passengers to miss getting home, traveling for work, and delayed for at least a day. In true Planes, Trains, and Automobiles fashion, some travellers set out to find alternative modes of transport as a result of the group stoppage.

items.title: Muse privacy invasions are freaking out Meta staffers, internal chats show
items.summary: After some early adopters of Meta’s Muse AI agent complained that it was spying on private messages and behaving unpredictably earlier this fall, Reuters exposed internal chats showing that Meta staff had raised the same alarms. When testing the agent, staff warned that Muse appeared to be accessing encrypted private messages that users did not expect the bot to review, could be mixing up conversations between users, and even potentially sharing sensitive information users would never expect to be exposed. items.title: The PSF end-of-year fundraiser
items.summary: The PSF end-of-year fundraiser With my Python Software Foundation board director hat on: we've launched our end-of-year fundraiser for the non-profit that supports Python development and the Python community. If your company or your work benefits from Python, please consider donating this year! items.title: Will Wright's next simulation will use AI to mine content from your memories
items.summary: The computer gaming world hasn't heard much from Will Wright ( SimCity, The Sims ) since the underwhelming release of Spore in 2008 and Wright's subsequent departure from Maxis owner EA. Now, well over 15 years later, Wright is starting to promote his next digital simulation, which will use generative AI technology to craft a game-like experience from players' memories. MyMems, which is slated to release next year, differentiates itself from Wright's previous projects by "turn the simulation inward," as Wright's Gallium Studios and partner Artificial Agency put it in a press release this morning.

items.title: This Huge US Ski Resort Has the World’s Most Reliable Snow, New Data Says
items.summary: In early November, the 2026 World Ski Awards handed out its winners, with only a few nods for ski resorts in North America. But a second ranking just came out, and while it doesn’t rate the best ski resorts, it rates something that may matter more to die-hard skiers: which resorts have the most reliable snowfall. The ranking comes from Inghams, a British travel company that has sold packaged ski trips since 1934. It ranked “reliable snow” — not just how much snow it gets, but how dependably lifts and runs stay open from one season to the next — at major ski resorts and regions using historical data rather than reputation.

items.title: How to Plan a Trip to the World’s Largest Ski Resort, Les Trois Vallées
items.summary: Standing at the top of a steep gully, I looked down at the line ahead. A handful of tracks cut through 10 inches of powder to my left, telling the story of the skiers who arrived before me. But I couldn’t help but notice untouched snow under an overhanging cliff face to my right. Before I dropped in, I looked out at the view ahead. I could make out tiny chairlift towers on the snow-capped peaks and ridgelines on the horizon. It felt as if the entire mountain range belonged to the Les Trois Vallées Ski Resort, one of the best—and the biggest—ski destinations in Europe.
